title: Korean-Style Grilled Duck Breast
shortDescription: Duck breasts are scored, marinated cold with pear, soy, garlic, and ginger, then grilled until the poultry-safe endpoint of 165°F / 74°C.
culturalContext: Duck is enjoyed in varied Korean preparations, including gui and bulgogi-style dishes. This is a contemporary Korean-style marinade applied to duck breast, not a claim of one canonical regional recipe.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Outdoor grill or approved electric grill

ingredients.preparation: skin scored without cutting into meat; do not wash

mixOrder: Stir in garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and pepper.
Coat chilled duck without contaminating reserved sauce.
marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: Nonreactive covered container at or below 40°F / 4°C
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 8 hours without test-cook approval.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Reserve any serving sauce before the marinade contacts raw duck.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard all marinade that contacted raw duck; do not brush it onto cooked meat.
substitutions: Use certified gluten-free tamari only after label verification.

instructions.heading: Score without washing
instructions.action: Keep duck cold, pat dry with disposable towels, and score only the skin in a shallow crosshatch; do not wash.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Skin is scored but flesh is not cut.
instructions.safetyNote: Treat duck as raw poultry and prevent sink and tool cross-contamination.

instructions.heading: Mix marinade
instructions.action: Combine marinade ingredients and reserve any serving sauce before raw contact.
instructions.safetyNote: Never serve marinade that has touched raw duck.

instructions.heading: Marinate cold
instructions.action: Coat duck, cover, and refrigerate for 2 hours.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Duck remains cold and evenly coated.
instructions.safetyNote: Never marinate poultry at room temperature.

instructions.heading: Prepare two zones
instructions.action: Preheat a medium direct zone and a cooler zone; remove duck from marinade and discard the marinade.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Grates are clean and lightly oiled.
instructions.safetyNote: Rendered duck fat can flare; keep the cooler zone available and never leave the grill.

instructions.heading: Grill and verify
instructions.action: Start skin-side down, move as needed to control flare-ups, turn, and cook until every breast reaches 165°F / 74°C in its thickest point.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Skin is browned and the thermometer reads at least 165°F / 74°C.
instructions.safetyNote: Visual color is not a safety test; use a calibrated thermometer.

instructions.heading: Rest and slice
instructions.action: Transfer with clean tongs to a clean platter, rest 5 minutes, then slice with a clean knife.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Juices settle and slices remain hot.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not return cooked duck to raw-contact serviceware.

grillSetup: Use an outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill with direct and cooler zones; expect rendered-fat flare-ups and keep raw and cooked tools separate.
targetInternalTemperature: 165°F / 74°C in the thickest part of every duck breast.
visualDonenessCues: Skin is browned without sustained flare-up charring
foodSafetyNotes: Duck is poultry: cook every breast to 165°F / 74°C.
Do not wash raw duck; prevent cross-contamination from hands, boards, knives, marinade, and towels.
Control rendered-fat flare-ups by moving duck to the cooler zone.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Verify every packaged-ingredient label and segregate tools for diners with allergies.

substitutions: Boneless chicken thigh is not a direct timing substitute; it still requires 165°F / 74°C.
Use certified gluten-free tamari only after label verification.
ingredientSourcing: Purchase duck cold from a reputable supplier and refrigerate promptly.
Choose intact packaging within its use-by date.
makeAhead: Mix marinade 1 day ahead; marinate duck only within the stated refrigerated range.
storage: Refrigerate cooked duck within 2 hours in a shallow covered container and use within 3 to 4 days.
leftovers: Slice only what will be served and refrigerate remaining cooked duck promptly.
servingSuggestions: Slice across the grain and serve with perilla leaves.

faq.question: Can duck breast be served medium?
faq.answer: Not in this safety-reviewed draft. Duck is poultry and the required endpoint is 165°F / 74°C.

faq.question: Can I reuse the marinade?
faq.answer: No. Discard marinade after it contacts raw duck.

metaDescription: Grill pear-soy marinated duck breast with two heat zones, flare-up control, strict raw-poultry separation, and a 165°F safety endpoint.
sourcesAndEditorialNotes: Editorial framing: contemporary Korean-style adaptation; naming requires Korean-language review.
